findings.evidence: The definition at lines 257–262 requires only TopologicalSpace M. A closed interval embedded in ℝ² has empty ambient interior, while its parametrized open interval is nonempty.
findings.fix: Call this the parametrized open cell; explain that it equals the ambient interior under the manifold hypotheses.
findings.issue: Here and at line 22, the image of the open ball is identified with the ambient interior, although IsCellularSet allows arbitrary topological spaces.

findings.evidence: isCellularSet_closedBall at line 299 permits r = 0; the fibre equivalences at lines 170 and 270 also permit singleton X.
findings.fix: Say that X is collapsed to one point and every other fibre is a singleton, or qualify nondegeneracy by assuming X has at least two points.
findings.issue: Lines 28, 54–56, 162–163 and 265–266 assert that X is a fibre with more than one point, but X may be a singleton.

summary: The cellular-set documentation overstates both the meaning of cell interiors and the existence of a nondegenerate fibre.
